purpose: Reduce retry amplification and ambiguous re-execution while preserving server-directed backpressure.

standards.title: 429 Too Many Requests
standards.repository_rule: Treat 429 as backpressure. Do not infer limiter scope or root cause.

standards.title: Retry-After
standards.repository_rule: A valid Retry-After value is a lower-bound timing signal. Never jitter earlier than it.

standards.title: Problem Details for HTTP APIs
standards.repository_rule: Use structured members for machine behavior. Do not scrape human detail text for retry logic.

standards.title: RateLimit header fields for HTTP
standards.repository_rule: May provide experimental quota/window hints. Keep draft semantics isolated from stable RFC behavior.

standards.title: The Idempotency-Key HTTP Header Field
standards.repository_rule: Do not assume universal Idempotency-Key semantics from this expired draft. Require an application/provider contract.

invariants: Retry-After is a floor; jitter may delay beyond it but never pull a retry earlier.
One logical recovery operation has one retry owner.
operation_id remains stable across retry attempts; attempt_id changes.
UNKNOWN operation outcome is not permission to re-execute.
Non-idempotent operations require explicit application/provider idempotency semantics before automatic re-execution.
First success after Blocked enters Recovering, not automatically Healthy.
Problem Details human-readable detail is not a machine control channel.
Draft RateLimit hints never override stronger stable server timing signals.

scheduler.formula: next_start = max(previous_start + minimum_period, now + retry_after_floor, now + local_backoff) + nonnegative_herd_jitter

draft_rate_limit_support.behavior: When r=0 and no stronger Retry-After is present, t may be used as an experimental minimum-delay hint.
draft_rate_limit_support.limitation: This is not a complete Structured Fields parser and does not claim RFC stability.
